_approach: Funky Drummer half-step: Clyde Stubblefield's original break barely states a backbeat at all - the groove lives in an off-kilter 16th ghost-snare pattern with the kick answering off the downbeat rather than locking to it. This approach keeps that half-stepped, ghost-heavy feel instead of jungle's usual dense amen chop-science, so the snare does most of the talking and the kick feels like it is chasing it. Ref: James Brown 'Funky Drummer' (Clyde Stubblefield); EDMProd's list of the three foundational jungle breaks (Amen, Think, Funky Drummer).
